iterations.theme: BiH i Srbija nakon izbora, politički islamizam među Bošnjacima te migracije i budućnost Europe

sections.subtitle: Od Tuzle do Praga: komentator, a ne novinar
sections.screenshot_description: Damir Omerbegović se predstavlja i opisuje čime se bavi
sections.content:
Nova epizoda podcasta **Ćušpajz** počinje predstavljanjem gosta. Voditelj ga najavljuje kao novinara, no **Damir Omerbegović** to odmah i odlučno opovrgava: „Nisam novinar, Bože dragi.“ Voditelj zato predlaže da se gost sam predstavi.

Omerbegović kaže da je rođen u **Tuzli**, a već godinama živi u **Pragu**. Bavi se društveno-političkim komentiranjem i pisanjem. U središtu njegova interesa su **Bosna i Hercegovina**, međunacionalni odnosi, bošnjački identitet te odnos religije i politike u bošnjačkom narodu.

Voditelj u šali objašnjava da je gosta namjerno odmah stavio pred izazov, kako bi provjerio je li se oporavio od viroze zbog koje je snimanje bilo odgođeno. Omerbegović ga uvjerava da je dobro, pa razgovor odmah prelazi na najaktualniju temu.
sections.subtitle_en: From Tuzla to Prague: a commentator, not a journalist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Damir Omerbegović introduces himself and describes what he does
sections.content_en:
The new episode of the podcast **Ćušpajz** begins with the introduction of the guest. The host introduces him as a journalist, but **Damir Omerbegović** immediately and decisively refutes this: "I am not a journalist, dear God." The host therefore suggests that the guest introduce himself.

Omerbegović says that he was born in **Tuzla**, and has been living in **Prague** for years. He is engaged in socio-political commentary and writing. At the center of his interest are **Bosnia and Herzegovina**, inter-ethnic relations, Bosniak identity, and the relationship between religion and politics among the Bosniak people.

The host jokingly explains that he intentionally challenged the guest right away, in order to check whether he had recovered from the virus due to which the recording had been postponed. Omerbegović assures him that he is well, so the conversation immediately moves to the most topical issue.

sections.subtitle: Pad Vučića: autokrata srušen demokratskim putem
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odaje priznanje studentima za uspjeh na izborima u Srbiji
sections.content:
Dok se dogovarao termin snimanja, u **Srbiji** su završili izbori. Voditelj pita je li i za gosta iznenađenje bio tako velik poraz **Vučića**, s tolikom razlikom u glasovima.

Omerbegović potvrđuje da je rezultat bio iznenađenje, ali ne baš u razmjerima u kojima se na kraju dogodio. Posebno ga raduje što se, kako kaže, **autokrata može srušiti demokratskim procesima, a ne nasilnim metodama**. Studentima odaje veliko priznanje. Ono što su postigli naziva nevjerojatnim i dodaje da takvo što nije viđeno godinama, ni u Europi ni u svijetu. Smatra da je to dobra vijest za cijelu regiju. Ipak, ostaje otvoreno kako će se razvijati srpsko društvo, koje i dalje ima problema, osobito s vlastitom poviješću.

Voditelj je skeptičniji. Ističe da su studenti bili vrlo dobro organizirani, da je cijela priča trajala gotovo dvije godine i da su se u medijima pojavljivale tvrdnje kako se radi o projektu stranih centara moći. Javnost je, kaže, tek u izbornoj noći doznala imena ljudi koji bi trebali preuzeti dužnosti. Njegovo je „skromno mišljenje“ da su bili uigrani i da to nije prošlo bez nečije pomoći.

Omerbegović uspjeh tumači drukčije. Studenti se po njemu nisu odmah pojavili kao još jedna tradicionalna politička organizacija. Godinama su se u Srbiji gledali sukobi vlasti i oporbe, a velik dio građana nije vjerovao ni jednima ni drugima. Studenti su krenuli od pitanja razumljivih gotovo svakome, potaknuti **tragedijom u Novom Sadu**:

- Tko je odgovoran kad se dogodi tragedija?
- Zašto institucije ne rade svoj posao?
- Zašto je potrebno izlaziti na ulice da bi se dobio odgovor na elementarna pitanja javne odgovornosti?

Tako su, zaključuje gost, povezali ljude koji se razilaze oko **Kosova, Rusije ili Europske unije**. Kad nastane takva društvena energija, ona može prerasti u ozbiljnu političku snagu.
sections.subtitle_en: The fall of Vučić: an autocrat overthrown democratically
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest credits students for success in the elections in Serbia
sections.content_en:
While the date for the recording was being arranged, the elections ended in **Serbia**. The host asks whether such a heavy defeat for **Vučić**, with such a margin in votes, was a surprise for the guest as well.

Omerbegović confirms that the result was a surprise, but not quite on the scale in which it ultimately occurred. He is particularly pleased that, as he says, **an autocrat can be overthrown through democratic processes, and not through violent methods**. He gives great credit to the students. What they achieved he calls incredible and adds that such a thing has not been seen for years, neither in Europe nor in the world. He considers this good news for the entire region. Nevertheless, it remains an open question how Serbian society will develop, which still has problems, especially with its own history.

The host is more skeptical. He points out that the students were very well organized, that the whole story lasted almost two years, and that claims appeared in the media that this was a project of foreign centers of power. The public, he says, only on election night learned the names of the people who were supposed to assume office. It is his "modest opinion" that they were well-drilled and that this did not happen without someone's help.

Omerbegović interprets the success differently. According to him, the students did not immediately appear as yet another traditional political organization. For years in Serbia, clashes between the government and the opposition were watched, and a large portion of citizens trusted neither. The students started from questions understandable to almost everyone, prompted by the **tragedy in Novi Sad**:

- Who is responsible when a tragedy occurs?
- Why are the institutions not doing their job?
- Why is it necessary to take to the streets to get an answer to elementary questions of public responsibility?

Thus, the guest concludes, they connected people who diverge over **Kosovo, Russia, or the European Union**. When such social energy is generated, it can grow into a serious political force.

sections.subtitle: Pobjednici bez lidera i ispit suočavanja s prošlošću
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o potrebi da nova srpska generacija prizna povijesne činjenice
sections.content:
Voditelj procjenjuje da s Vučićem još nije gotovo. Naglašava da time ne želi stati na njegovu stranu, nego realno sagledati situaciju. Ljudi sa studentske liste davali su, kaže, svakakve izjave o **Hrvatskoj, Bosni i Hercegovini i Kosovu**, pa ništa još nije definirano. Ponavlja ono što je rekao i jednom od ranijih gostiju: pobjednici još nisu svjesni da su pobijedili ni kakav ih golem posao čeka.

Omerbegović se slaže da studenti još nemaju jasnog lidera ni kandidata za premijera, kao ni organiziranu strukturu kakvu imaju političke stranke. Ipak, smatra da moraju krenuti prema **potpunoj demokratizaciji društva**, koja uključuje ozbiljniji odnos prema prošlosti. Otvoreno kaže da je upravo to razlog zbog kojeg se o srpskim izborima toliko govori u Hrvatskoj i BiH.

Pri tome inzistira na preciznosti. Današnje mlade generacije u Srbiji **nisu odgovorne ni za što** od zločina počinjenih prije njihova rođenja. Prvi korak vidi u **priznavanju povijesnih činjenica**, uz jasno izbjegavanje prihvaćanja kolektivne krivnje. Primjećuje da se o tome već intenzivnije govori u nekim sarajevskim medijima.

Zanima ga hoće li nova politička generacija biti spremna otvoreno govoriti o tim temama bez straha da će je netko optužiti za izdaju Srbije. Navodi da je **Ilija Srdanović**, vjerojatni budući premijer, u prvim razgovorima naglašavao poštivanje sudskih presuda i potrebu za drukčijim odnosima u regiji. Tu poruku smatra vrlo relevantnom, ali dodaje da će se konkretne promjene moći ocijeniti tek kroz buduće odluke i politiku.
sections.subtitle_en: Winners without a leader and the test of facing the past
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest talks about the need for the new Serbian generation to acknowledge historical facts
sections.content_en:
The host assesses that it is not yet over with Vučić. He emphasizes that by this he does not want to take his side, but to view the situation realistically. People from the student list made, he says, all kinds of statements about **Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Kosovo**, so nothing is yet defined. He repeats what he also told one of the earlier guests: the winners are not yet aware that they have won, nor what enormous work awaits them.

Omerbegović agrees that the students do not yet have a clear leader or candidate for prime minister, nor an organized structure such as political parties have. Nevertheless, he considers that they must move toward the **complete democratization of society**, which includes a more serious attitude toward the past. He says openly that this is precisely the reason why the Serbian elections are being talked about so much in Croatia and BiH.

In doing so, he insists on precision. Today's young generations in Serbia **are not responsible for anything** regarding the crimes committed before their birth. He sees the first step in **acknowledging historical facts**, with a clear avoidance of accepting collective guilt. He notes that this is already being discussed more intensively in some Sarajevo media.

He wonders whether the new political generation will be ready to speak openly about these topics without fear that someone will accuse them of betraying Serbia. He mentions that **Ilija Srdanović**, the probable future prime minister, emphasized in early conversations the respect for court rulings and the need for different relations in the region. He considers that message very relevant, but adds that concrete changes can be evaluated only through future decisions and policy.

sections.subtitle: Izbori u BiH: pobjeda na izborima nije isto što i stvarna moć
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava razliku između izborne pobjede i stvarne političke moći u BiH
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da su srpski izbori zasjenili jednako važne izbore u **Bosni i Hercegovini**, održane otprilike mjesec dana ranije. Najviše ga se dojmila organizacija: izbori su provedeni elektronički i transparentno, onako kako to mnogi traže u Hrvatskoj, a vjerojatno i u Srbiji. Smatra da je **visoki predstavnik** tu odigrao ono što je morao. Gosta zatim pita tko je konačni pobjednik, a tko gubitnik.

Omerbegović priznaje da je to vrlo teško pitanje. Prvo treba razlikovati **izbornu pobjedu od stvarne političke moći**, jer to u BiH nisu nužno iste stvari. Rezultate iznosi za sve tri strane:

- **SDA**, najveća bošnjačka stranka od kraja 90-ih, ponovno je ostvarila značajan rezultat: 9 zastupnika u državnom parlamentu i 31 u Zastupničkom domu Parlamenta Federacije. Zato se, kaže, ne može govoriti o političkoj marginalizaciji o kojoj se pričalo proteklih godina.
- **HDZ** je ostvario važnu pobjedu izborom **Darijane Filipović** u Predsjedništvo, što je značajno za hrvatsku političku scenu.
- **SNSD** je zadržao ozbiljnu parlamentarnu snagu u **Republici Srpskoj** i na državnoj razini.

U tome Omerbegović vidi srž bosanskohercegovačkog političkog sustava: stranka može imati odličan rezultat, a ipak ne može formirati vlast bez onih koje je do jučer kritizirala i nazivala svakakvim imenima.
sections.subtitle_en: Elections in BiH: winning the elections is not the same as actual power
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the difference between electoral victory and actual political power in BiH
sections.content_en:
The host observes that the Serbian elections overshadowed the equally important elections in **Bosnia and Herzegovina**, held about a month earlier. He was most impressed by the organization: the elections were conducted electronically and transparently, the way many demand in Croatia, and probably in Serbia as well. He believes that the **High Representative** played what he had to play there. He then asks the guest who the ultimate winner is, and who the loser.

Omerbegović admits that this is a very difficult question. First, one must distinguish **electoral victory from actual political power**, because in BiH these are not necessarily the same things. He presents the results for all three sides:

- **SDA**, the largest Bosniak party since the late 1990s, once again achieved a significant result: 9 representatives in the state parliament and 31 in the House of Representatives of the Parliament of the Federation. Therefore, he says, one cannot speak of the political marginalization that was talked about in recent years.
- **HDZ** achieved an important victory with the election of **Darijana Filipović** to the Presidency, which is significant for the Croatian political scene.
- **SNSD** retained serious parliamentary strength in **Republika Srpska** and at the state level.

In this Omerbegović sees the core of the Bosnia and Herzegovina political system: a party can have an excellent result, and yet cannot form a government without those whom it criticized and called all sorts of names until yesterday.

sections.subtitle: Bakir Izetbegović nikada nije ni otišao
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o važnosti Bakira Izetbegovića u bošnjačkoj politici
sections.content:
Voditelj pita znače li ovi izbori povratak **Bakira Izetbegovića**. Omerbegović smatra da Izetbegović nikada nije ni izašao iz politike ni izgubio važnost na bošnjačkoj političkoj sceni. To što ponekad izgubi utrku za Predsjedništvo ne znači da nije bitan faktor. Kao dokaz navodi da je **Čović** nedavno razgovarao upravo s njim. Voditelj dodaje da je razgovarao i s **Nerminom Nikšićem**, što gost potvrđuje.

Omerbegović naglašava da su u zemlji kakva je BiH politički razgovori među različitim strankama nužni. Očekuje da će Bakir Izetbegović u sljedeće četiri godine biti vrlo važan faktor u svemu što se bude događalo u bošnjačkoj politici.

Na voditeljevu primjedbu da se još ne zna tko je pobijedio, uz ironično „dobra stara Bosna“, gost odgovara kratko: „Pobijedili su političari.“ Kad voditelj doda da je narod vjerojatno ponovno najviše izgubio, Omerbegović uzvraća: „Pa, narod ih je izabrao. Hajde da se ne lažemo.“
sections.subtitle_en: Bakir Izetbegović never even left
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest talks about the importance of Bakir Izetbegović in Bosniak politics
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether these elections mean the return of **Bakir Izetbegović**. Omerbegović considers that Izetbegović never left politics nor lost importance on the Bosniak political scene. The fact that he sometimes loses the race for the Presidency does not mean he is not an important factor. As proof, he cites that **Čović** recently spoke with him specifically. The host adds that he also spoke with **Nermin Nikšić**, which the guest confirms.

Omerbegović emphasizes that in a country such as BiH, political talks among different parties are necessary. He expects that Bakir Izetbegović will be a very important factor in everything that happens in Bosniak politics over the next four years.

To the host's remark that it is not yet known who won, along with an ironic "good old Bosnia", the guest replies briefly: "The politicians won." When the host adds that the people probably lost the most again, Omerbegović counters: "Well, the people elected them. Let's not kid ourselves."

sections.subtitle: Što poraz Vučića znači za Republiku Srpsku i Dodika
sections.screenshot_description: Gost procjenjuje utjecaj srpskih izbora na odnose s BiH i Republikom Srpskom
sections.content:
Voditelj vraća razgovor na Srbiju i pita kako će se izborni rezultat odraziti na **Republiku Srpsku** i **Dodika**, kojega je, kako kaže, u politički život vratio **Trump**. Dodaje da Dodiku Vučićev poraz zasigurno ne odgovara.

Omerbegović je oprezan. Još nije jasno kakva će biti politika u Srbiji, pa ni kakva će biti politika prema Republici Srpskoj. Kad bi morao dati projekciju, rekao bi da studentska pobjeda **može promijeniti cijeli odnos prema Bosni i Hercegovini** i otvoriti nove mogućnosti. Ipak, ne bi unaprijed najavljivao velike promjene, ni prema BiH ni prema Republici Srpskoj.

Naglašava, i sam priznaje da to stalno ponavlja, da tek treba vidjeti kakvu će politiku nova vlast doista voditi. Srbija ima **dugoročne institucionalne i političke interese** koji ne ovise o jednoj osobi. Odnosi s Republikom Srpskom, pitanje Kosova koje je otvoreno desetljećima, položaj Srba u regiji i odnosi s velikim silama ostat će, po njegovu sudu, sasvim sigurno važne teme.
sections.subtitle_en: What the defeat of Vučić means for Republika Srpska and Dodik
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest assesses the impact of Serbian elections on relations with BiH and Republika Srpska
sections.content_en:
The host turns the conversation back to Serbia and asks how the election result will affect **Republika Srpska** and **Dodik**, who, as he says, was brought back into political life by **Trump**. He adds that Vučić's defeat certainly does not suit Dodik.

Omerbegović is cautious. It is not yet clear what the policy in Serbia will be like, nor what the policy toward Republika Srpska will be like. If he had to make a projection, he would say that the students' victory **can change the entire relationship toward Bosnia and Herzegovina** and open new possibilities. Still, he would not announce major changes in advance, neither toward BiH nor toward Republika Srpska.

He emphasizes, and admits himself that he repeats this constantly, that it remains to be seen what policy the new government will actually pursue. Serbia has **long-term institutional and political interests** that do not depend on one person. Relations with Republika Srpska, the Kosovo issue that has been open for decades, the position of Serbs in the region, and relations with the great powers will, in his judgment, quite certainly remain important topics.

sections.subtitle: Lista želja za novu vlast: EU, izborni zakon i OHR
sections.screenshot_description: Gost nabraja prioritete nove vlasti u BiH
sections.content:
Voditelj traži tri konkretna poteza koja bi nova vlast u BiH morala povući u prvih 12 mjeseci. Omerbegović nudi svoju, kako je naziva, **„wish listu“**:

1. **Brži put prema Europskoj uniji.** Proces pristupanja bio je u protekle četiri godine vrlo trom, bez stvarnog napretka. Gost vjeruje da je upravo to jedan od razloga zbog kojih su birači, osobito Bošnjaci, glasovali onako kako su glasovali.
2. **Izmjene izbornog zakona**, ključne za samo funkcioniranje države.
3. **Rješavanje pitanja OHR-a** i njegove važnosti za budućnost BiH.

O trećoj točki, kaže, govori već dugo. Smatra da se o tome mora otvoreno razgovarati kako bi BiH napokon postala država svih njezinih naroda, u kojoj će oni sami donositi važne političke odluke o vlastitoj budućnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Wish list for the new government: EU, election law, and OHR
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest lists the priorities of the new government in BiH
sections.content_en:
The host asks for three concrete moves that the new government in BiH should make in the first 12 months. Omerbegović offers his, as he calls it, **"wish list"**:

1. **A faster path toward the European Union.** The accession process has been very sluggish over the past four years, without real progress. The guest believes that this is precisely one of the reasons why voters, especially Bosniaks, voted the way they did.
2. **Amendments to the election law**, crucial for the very functioning of the state.
3. **Resolving the issue of the OHR** and its importance for the future of BiH.

Regarding the third point, he says, he has been speaking for a long time. He believes that this must be discussed openly so that BiH finally becomes a state of all its peoples, in which they themselves will make important political decisions about their own future.

sections.subtitle: Dayton je zaustavio rat, ali nije kriv za sve
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o političkoj kulturi u kojoj se kompromis smatra izdajom
sections.content:
Voditelj se pita je li za stanje u BiH kriv **Daytonski sporazum** ili činjenica da se političke elite nikada nisu do kraja dogovorile kakvu državu žele, nego rade svoje „ispod pulta“.

Omerbegović upozorava na oprez. Dayton je zaustavio rat, ali je stvorio ustavnu strukturu koja je i danas izuzetno složena, i obje te činjenice treba priznati. Ipak, ne misli da je svaki problem posljedica Daytona. Problem vidi u **političkoj kulturi u kojoj se kompromis predstavlja kao izdaja, a institucionalna blokada kao patriotska pobjeda**.

Može se, kaže, napisati mnogo jednostavniji ustav, ali ako politički akteri nemaju ni minimum međusobnog povjerenja, ni takav ustav neće sam riješiti probleme. Zato ustavne reforme moraju ići zajedno s promjenom političke prakse.

Kao konkretan put predlaže da se ponovno ozbiljno prouči iskustvo **aprilskog paketa iz 2006.** To je, prema njegovim riječima, posljednji put da su institucije BiH gotovo jednoglasno pokušale promijeniti strukturu države. Paket nije bio savršen, ali je bio pokušaj da se postojeći ustavni sustav učini funkcionalnijim. Omerbegović zaključuje da bi radije vidio nekoliko ostvarivih reformi nego još 20 godina rasprava o idealnom ustavu koji nitko nije spreman prihvatiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Dayton stopped the war, but is not to blame for everything
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest talks about a political culture in which compromise is considered treason
sections.content_en:
The host wonders whether the situation in BiH is the fault of the **Dayton Agreement** or the fact that political elites never fully agreed on what kind of state they want, but do their own things "under the table".

Omerbegović advises caution. Dayton stopped the war, but it created a constitutional structure that is exceptionally complex even today, and both of these facts should be acknowledged. Nevertheless, he does not think that every problem is a consequence of Dayton. He sees the problem in a **political culture in which compromise is presented as treason, and institutional blockade as a patriotic victory**.

A much simpler constitution can be written, he says, but if political actors lack even a minimum of mutual trust, even such a constitution will not solve the problems on its own. Therefore, constitutional reforms must go hand in hand with a change in political practice.

As a concrete path, he proposes a serious re-examination of the experience of the **April package from 2006**. That was, according to him, the last time that the institutions of BiH almost unanimously attempted to change the structure of the state. The package was not perfect, but it was an attempt to make the existing constitutional system more functional. Omerbegović concludes that he would rather see several achievable reforms than another 20 years of debates about an ideal constitution that no one is ready to accept.

sections.subtitle: SDA i HDZ: stari partneri i topli odnosi
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o odnosima Bakira Izetbegovića i Dragana Čovića
sections.content:
Voditelj pita kakvi će biti odnosi Hrvata i Bošnjaka nakon što je **Komšić** otišao u svojevrsnu političku mirovinu, jer je s hrvatske strane oko njega bilo dosta problema. Zanima ga hoće li odnos SDA i HDZ-a sada biti bolji.

Omerbegović podsjeća da su **SDA i HDZ** već nekoliko puta bili partneri u vlasti, pa ne bi bilo nikakvo čudo da to ponovno postanu. Smatra da **Bakir Izetbegović i Dragan Čović** imaju prilično tople odnose, što se vidi iz njihovih zajedničkih izjava i nastupa, te da među njima nema velikog neprijateljstva.

Najvažnije mu je da sve tri strane u BiH prihvaćaju kompromise. Prihvaćanje kompromisa, dodaje, ne znači da druge strane odustaju od svojih zahtjeva. Od bošnjačke politike očekuje da prihvati potrebu za **konkretnim institucionalnim mehanizmima koji štite kolektivna prava Hrvata i Srba**, o čemu se govorilo u kontekstu izbornog zakona. Nada se i da će se Bošnjaci nakon ovih izbora prestati toliko hvaliti svojom brojčanom nadmoći u Federaciji i u BiH.
sections.subtitle_en: SDA and HDZ: old partners and warm relations
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about relations between Bakir Izetbegović and Dragan Čović
sections.content_en:
The host asks what the relations between Croats and Bosniaks will be like after **Komšić** went into a kind of political retirement, since on the Croatian side there were quite a few problems surrounding him. He wonders whether the relationship between SDA and HDZ will now be better.

Omerbegović recalls that **SDA and HDZ** have already been partners in government several times, so it would be no wonder if they became that again. He considers that **Bakir Izetbegović and Dragan Čović** have quite warm relations, which can be seen from their joint statements and appearances, and that there is no great hostility between them.

The most important thing for him is that all three sides in BiH accept compromises. Accepting compromises, he adds, does not mean that the other sides give up their demands. From Bosniak politics, he expects acceptance of the need for **concrete institutional mechanisms that protect the collective rights of Croats and Serbs**, which was discussed in the context of the election law. He also hopes that after these elections Bosniaks will stop boasting so much about their numerical superiority in the Federation and in BiH.

sections.subtitle: Što je zapravo politički islamizam
sections.screenshot_description: Gost definira pojam političkog islamizma
sections.content:
Razgovor prelazi na temu kojom se Omerbegović, kako mu voditelj napominje, posebno bavi: politički aktivizam i radikalizam među Bošnjacima. Gost objašnjava da se **islamizmom među Bošnjacima** bavi dugo i da taj fenomen ima tragove i izvan granica BiH.

Najprije želi definirati pojmove. Kad govori o islamizmu, ne govori o islamu kao religiji ni o muslimanima kao ljudima, nego o **političkoj ideologiji koja nastoji određeno tumačenje islama pretvoriti u temelj političkog i društvenog poretka**.

Islamizam, naglašava, nije jedinstven fenomen. Postoje različiti pokreti, organizacije i političke škole:

- neki djeluju kroz institucionalnu politiku,
- neki kroz društveni aktivizam,
- određeni ekstremistički pokreti zagovaraju ili koriste nasilje, čega je u BiH bilo u posljednjih 30 godina, od potpisivanja Daytonskog sporazuma.

Te se kategorije, prema njegovu mišljenju, ne smiju poistovjećivati. Središnje pitanje za njega je odnos religije i političke vlasti. Svaki čovjek mora imati slobodu prakticirati svoju religiju, ali i slobodu da ne prakticira nijednu, da promijeni vjeru i da ne bude podvrgnut političkim pravilima koja proizlaze iz tuđih vjerskih uvjerenja. Zbog toga vidi potrebu za ozbiljnom raspravom o političkom islamizmu među Bošnjacima, u BiH i izvan nje.
sections.subtitle_en: What political Islamism actually is
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest defines the concept of political Islamism
sections.content_en:
The conversation moves to the topic with which Omerbegović, as the host notes, particularly deals: political activism and radicalism among Bosniaks. The guest explains that he has been dealing with **Islamism among Bosniaks** for a long time and that this phenomenon has traces outside the borders of BiH as well.

First, he wants to define terms. When speaking of Islamism, he does not speak of Islam as a religion nor of Muslims as people, but of a **political ideology that seeks to turn a certain interpretation of Islam into the foundation of the political and social order**.

Islamism, he emphasizes, is not a unified phenomenon. There are different movements, organizations, and political schools:

- some act through institutional politics,
- some through social activism,
- certain extremist movements advocate or use violence, of which there has been in BiH in the last 30 years, since the signing of the Dayton Agreement.

These categories, in his opinion, must not be equated. The central question for him is the relationship between religion and political power. Every person must have the freedom to practice their religion, but also the freedom not to practice any, to change faith, and not to be subjected to political rules deriving from someone else's religious convictions. Because of this, he sees the need for a serious discussion about political Islamism among Bosniaks, in BiH and outside it.

sections.subtitle: Zid šutnje: otpor raspravi o islamizmu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje otpor na koji nailazi kad otvara temu islamizma
sections.content:
Na pitanje postoji li volja za takvu raspravu, Omerbegović odgovara: „Nažalost, još uvijek ne.“ Posebno u posljednjih godinu dana pokušava otvoriti tu temu u BiH, ali nailazi na velik otpor.

Otpor ne dolazi samo od propagandista i islamista čija su imena, kaže, dobro poznata na internetu i u stvarnom životu. Dolazi i od ljudi koji nisu islamisti i predstavljaju se kao **progresivni Bošnjaci**, a djeluju u medijskim i političkim krugovima. I oni, prema njegovim riječima, pokušavaju sve „gurnuti pod tepih“, kao da će problem nestati sam od sebe ako se o njemu ne govori.

Problemi su, upozorava, svake godine sve veći. Ne misli nužno na terorističke napade ili ekstremističke prijetnje koje ugrožavaju sigurnost, nego na atmosferu u javnom prostoru. Čitateljima i slušateljima poručuje da otvore bošnjačke portale i pogledaju vijesti o **Izraelu i Iranu**, pa će vidjeti o čemu govori.
sections.subtitle_en: Wall of silence: resistance to discussing Islamism
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the resistance he encounters when opening the topic of Islamism
sections.content_en:
To the question of whether there is a willingness for such a discussion, Omerbegović replies: "Unfortunately, still not." Especially over the past year, he has been trying to open that topic in BiH, but encounters great resistance.

The resistance does not come only from propagandists and Islamists whose names, he says, are well known on the internet and in real life. It also comes from people who are not Islamists and present themselves as **progressive Bosniaks**, acting in media and political circles. They too, according to him, try to sweep everything "under the carpet", as if the problem will disappear on its own if it is not talked about.

The problems, he warns, are growing greater every year. He does not necessarily mean terrorist attacks or extremist threats that endanger security, but rather the atmosphere in the public space. He tells readers and listeners to open Bosniak portals and look at the news about **Israel and Iran**, and they will see what he is talking about.

sections.subtitle: Islamist nije terorist, a Bošnjaci su sekularan narod
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava da Bošnjaci nisu islamisti i govori o sekulariziranosti
sections.content:
Voditelj se pita zašto se islamizam odmah povezuje s radikalizmom i zašto se islamist odmah zamišlja kao „čovjek koji nosi bombu“. Omerbegović se slaže da **islamist ne znači terorist**. Jednako jasno naglašava da ne tvrdi kako su **Bošnjaci kao narod islamisti** niti da većina Bošnjaka želi šerijatski zakon ili islamsku državu.

Priznaje da relevantnih i svježih podataka o broju Bošnjaka s radikalnim političkim stavovima nema. Posljednja anketa provedena je prije otprilike 13 godina. Tada je **oko 15 posto ispitanika** reklo da bi rado vidjelo šerijatsku državu, što gost smatra malim udjelom.

Voditelj pita što bi Bošnjaci, mimo velikih geopolitičkih planova o „šerijatskoj državi u srcu Europe“, uopće mislili da bi time dobili. Omerbegović sumnja da većina njih uopće zna što je šerijatska država. Bošnjake opisuje kao **vrlo sekulariziran narod**, nominalno muslimanski. Većina ide u džamiju uglavnom na **bajramske namaze**, što smatra sasvim korektnim, a pri recitiranju na arapskom ne razumije što izgovara.

Istodobno primjećuje sve snažnije arapske utjecaje. Njihove nositelje, „ne podrugljivo, nego malo iz šale“, naziva **„milk šejhovima“**: to su bradati propovjednici koji recitiraju sure na arapskom i očekuju da će ih Bošnjaci slijediti. To se, kaže, još nije dogodilo.
sections.subtitle_en: An Islamist is not a terrorist, and Bosniaks are a secular people
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains that Bosniaks are not Islamists and talks about secularization
sections.content_en:
The host wonders why Islamism is immediately associated with radicalism and why an Islamist is immediately imagined as a "man carrying a bomb". Omerbegović agrees that **an Islamist does not mean a terrorist**. Equally clearly, he emphasizes that he does not claim that **Bosniaks as a people are Islamists**, nor that the majority of Bosniaks want Sharia law or an Islamic state.

He admits that there are no relevant and fresh data on the number of Bosniaks with radical political views. The last poll was conducted about 13 years ago. At that time, **around 15 percent of respondents** said that they would gladly see a Sharia state, which the guest considers a small share.

The host asks what Bosniaks, beyond grand geopolitical plans for a "Sharia state in the heart of Europe", would think they would gain from that at all. Omerbegović doubts that most of them even know what a Sharia state is. He describes Bosniaks as a **very secularized people**, nominally Muslim. Most go to the mosque mainly for **Eid prayers**, which he considers completely fine, and during recitation in Arabic do not understand what they are uttering.

At the same time, he notices increasingly stronger Arab influences. Their proponents, "not mockingly, but a bit in jest", he calls **"milk sheikhs"**: these are bearded preachers who recite surahs in Arabic and expect Bosniaks to follow them. That, he says, has not happened yet.

sections.subtitle: Mudžahedini, Sirija i Islamska deklaracija Alije Izetbegovića
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o Islamskoj deklaraciji Alije Izetbegovića iz 1970.
sections.content:
Omerbegović pojašnjava da mu nije riječ o vjerskoj praksi nego o **prisutnosti određenih političkih i ideoloških struja** u društvu. Bošnjaci, kaže, imaju dugu povijest političkog islama, s ideološkim tekstovima i organizacijama. Nabraja nekoliko pojava:

- dolazak **stranih mudžahedina** tijekom rata, o čemu se danas gotovo i ne govori,
- poslijeratne probleme s radikalizacijom,
- konkretne slučajeve odlaska državljana BiH na **strana ratišta**, osobito u **Siriju** prije desetak godina.

Ne tvrdi da te pojave imaju iste uzroke ili ciljeve, a dodaje i da većina Bošnjaka ne zna zašto su ti ljudi otišli ratovati u Siriju.

Voditelj, koji kaže da je i sam prošao rat, nudi drukčiju perspektivu. I mnogi Hrvati i Srbi otišli su u Ukrajinu, svaki na svoju stranu. Shvaća da je u ratu, kad su Bošnjaci bili „stisnuti u procjepu“ i kad je svatko ratovao sa svakim, svaka pomoć bila dobrodošla. Pretpostavlja da su jače sile odredile da mudžahedini ostanu i prošire utjecaj, pa ni **rahmetli Alija** možda tu nije mogao mnogo učiniti.

Omerbegović se ne slaže. Alija Izetbegović imao je, kaže, duboke povijesne veze s islamističkim pokretima i nemoguće je ozbiljno govoriti o povijesti političkog islamizma među Bošnjacima, a zanemariti njegovu **Islamsku deklaraciju iz 1970.** Taj tekst bavi se islamizacijom muslimanskih društava i ulogom islama u oblikovanju političkog i društvenog života. Gost naglašava da deklaracija nije bila ustavni nacrt za buduću neovisnu BiH i da o njezinu sadržaju i kontekstu postoje ozbiljne akademske rasprave. Jedni u njoj prepoznaju elemente političkog islamizma, a drugi ističu da se bavila širim muslimanskim svijetom, a ne projektom islamske države u BiH.

Upravo zato taj tekst smatra ključnim za razumijevanje današnje situacije. Ne može se proglasiti nevažnim za biografiju autora, ali se ni cjelokupna povijesna uloga Alije Izetbegovića ne smije svesti na njega. Njegovu ulogu u borbi za neovisnost BiH moguće je priznati i istodobno kritički analizirati njegove ideološke stavove. „U zdravom društvu to ne bi trebalo biti ništa sporno, ali eto, još uvijek kod Bošnjaka jest“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Mujahideen, Syria, and Alija Izetbegović's Islamic Declaration
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about Alija Izetbegović's Islamic Declaration from 1970
sections.content_en:
Omerbegović clarifies that his point is not religious practice, but the **presence of certain political and ideological currents** in society. Bosniaks, he says, have a long history of political Islam, with ideological texts and organizations. He lists several phenomena:

- the arrival of **foreign mujahideen** during the war, which is hardly talked about today,
- post-war problems with radicalization,
- concrete cases of BiH citizens departing for **foreign battlefields**, especially to **Syria** about ten years ago.

He does not claim that these phenomena have the same causes or goals, and he also adds that the majority of Bosniaks do not know why those people went to fight in Syria.

The host, who says that he himself lived through the war, offers a different perspective. Many Croats and Serbs also went to Ukraine, each to their own side. He understands that in the war, when Bosniaks were "caught in a squeeze" and when everyone fought everyone, any help was welcome. He presumes that stronger powers determined that the mujahideen remain and expand their influence, so even **the late Alija** perhaps could not do much there.

Omerbegović disagrees. Alija Izetbegović had, he says, deep historical ties with Islamist movements, and it is impossible to speak seriously about the history of political Islamism among Bosniaks while ignoring his **Islamic Declaration from 1970**. That text deals with the Islamization of Muslim societies and the role of Islam in shaping political and social life. The guest emphasizes that the declaration was not a constitutional blueprint for a future independent BiH and that there are serious academic debates about its content and context. Some recognize elements of political Islamism in it, while others point out that it dealt with the broader Muslim world, not with the project of an Islamic state in BiH.

Precisely for this reason, he considers that text crucial for understanding today's situation. It cannot be declared irrelevant to the author's biography, but neither should the overall historical role of Alija Izetbegović be reduced to it. It is possible to acknowledge his role in the fight for the independence of BiH and at the same time critically analyze his ideological positions. "In a healthy society that should not be controversial at all, but well, among Bosniaks it still is," he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Tursko pitanje i neslaganje s Fatmirom Ali Spahićem
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto se ne slaže s tezom o presudnom utjecaju stranih sila
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da u BiH postoji sukob između ideologije koja negira demokraciju i ljudi koji je žele. Zatim pita koliki utjecaj ima **Turska**, podsjećajući da je raniji gost podcasta, **Fatmir Ali Spahić**, govorio o snažnom turskom utjecaju i o **Erdoganu**.

Omerbegović kaže da je upravo prije snimanja slušao tu epizodu i da se s Ali Spahićem u mnogočemu ne slaže, osobito oko stranih utjecaja. Ne želi ga previše kritizirati jer ga smatra jednim od rijetkih s kojima bi volio razgovarati licem u lice.

Glavni mu je prigovor tezi o presudnom utjecaju stranih sila, agencija ili „mračnih sila“ da Bošnjacima **oduzima samostalnost**, odnosno intelektualnu sposobnost da sami biraju koje će pravce slijediti, a koje odbaciti. Ne smatra da većina utjecaja dolazi iz Turske, Irana ili od drugih vanjskih aktera, iako i njih često kritizira.

Po njegovu tumačenju, Bošnjaci promatraju geopolitičku situaciju i pokušavaju pronaći svoje mjesto u svijetu. Slušaju **Milorada Dodika** kako govori o muslimanima, slušaju krajnje desne politike iz EU-a i **SAD-a** i s njima ne nalaze zajednički jezik. Zato neki počnu gledati prema **Iranu, Venezueli s Madurom ili Rusiji s Putinom** kao prema alternativi desničarskim pokretima, Dodiku ili Izraelu. Ključni problem, zaključuje, jest to što se Bošnjaci pokušavaju snaći u svijetu koji ne razumiju, a ni svijet njih ne razumije najbolje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Turkish question and disagreement with Fatmir Ali Spahić
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why he disagrees with the thesis about the decisive influence of foreign powers
sections.content_en:
The host observes that in BiH there is a conflict between an ideology that denies democracy and people who want it. Then he asks how much influence **Turkey** has, recalling that an earlier guest on the podcast, **Fatmir Ali Spahić**, spoke of strong Turkish influence and of **Erdogan**.

Omerbegović says that he listened to that episode right before recording and that he disagrees with Ali Spahić on many things, especially regarding foreign influences. He does not want to criticize him too much because he considers him one of the few with whom he would like to speak face to face.

His main objection to the thesis about the decisive influence of foreign powers, agencies, or "dark forces" is that it **deprives Bosniaks of agency**, that is, the intellectual capacity to choose for themselves which directions to follow and which to reject. He does not think that most of the influence comes from Turkey, Iran, or other external actors, although he frequently criticizes them as well.

According to his interpretation, Bosniaks observe the geopolitical situation and try to find their place in the world. They listen to **Milorad Dodik** speaking about Muslims, they listen to far-right policies from the EU and the **United States**, and they find no common language with them. That is why some start looking toward **Iran, Venezuela with Maduro, or Russia with Putin** as an alternative to right-wing movements, Dodik, or Israel. The key problem, he concludes, is that Bosniaks are trying to find their way in a world they do not understand, nor does the world understand them best.

sections.subtitle: Multietnička BiH čvrsto ukorijenjena na Zapadu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost iznosi svoju viziju multietničke BiH u Europskoj uniji
sections.content:
Voditelj kaže da bi se najradije vratio u BiH s kraja 80-ih, kakvu on pamti. Omerbegović odgovara da svatko ima svoje mišljenje, a na pitanje kakvo bi bilo njegovo rješenje odgovara bez oklijevanja: želi **multietničku Bosnu i Hercegovinu u Europskoj uniji, duboko ukorijenjenu na Zapadu**.

Voditelj podsjeća da obojica žive u EU-u i znaju da „nije sve zlatno“. Gost to priznaje, ali dodaje: „I ova hrđa puno je sjajnija ovdje u Europskoj uniji nego u Bosni i Hercegovini.“
sections.subtitle_en: Multiethnic BiH firmly rooted in the West
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest presents his vision of a multiethnic BiH in the European Union
sections.content_en:
The host says that he would most like to return to the BiH of the late 1980s, as he remembers it. Omerbegović replies that everyone has their opinion, and to the question of what his solution would be, he replies without hesitation: he wants a **multiethnic Bosnia and Herzegovina in the European Union, deeply rooted in the West**.

The host recalls that both live in the EU and know that "not all is golden". The guest admits this, but adds: "Even this rust is much shinier here in the European Union than in Bosnia and Herzegovina."

sections.subtitle: Češki model: pragmatičnost umjesto zapaljenih automobila
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje pragmatičan pristup Češke migracijama
sections.content:
Razgovor prelazi na migracije, strane radnike i ilegalne migrante. Voditelj pita kakvo je stanje u **Češkoj**.

Omerbegović Češku opisuje kao **vrlo pragmatičnu zemlju** sa strogim uvjetima za boravak i rad, što zna iz vlastitog iskustva. U šali dodaje da ima „kamaru“ komičnih priča o češkim institucijama, ali da je to tema za neki drugi put.

Razlika između **Praga i Pariza** mu je očita. Iz Praga ne stižu vijesti o velikim neredima ni o zastavama koje nisu ni europske ni češke. Kad je prije 10 do 15 godina krenuo migrantski val, **Češka, Slovačka, Poljska i Mađarska** imale su pragmatičan pristup. Bile su osuđivane zbog rasizma i „nemilosrdnog“ odnosa prema migrantima, ali danas, ističe gost, nemaju problema s tjednim paljenjem automobila i trgovina.

Drago mu je što živi u takvoj državi, i to u praškoj četvrti u kojoj žive legalni migranti. Smatra da bi Europska unija, Europa, pa i svijet, trebali od Češke preuzeti mnogo toga.
sections.subtitle_en: The Czech model: pragmatism instead of torched cars
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes the Czech Republic's pragmatic approach to migration
sections.content_en:
The conversation moves to migration, foreign workers, and illegal migrants. The host asks what the situation is like in the **Czech Republic**.

Omerbegović describes the Czech Republic as a **very pragmatic country** with strict conditions for stay and work, which he knows from his own experience. He jokingly adds that he has a "heap" of comical stories about Czech institutions, but that this is a topic for another time.

The difference between **Prague and Paris** is obvious to him. From Prague there is no news of major riots or of flags that are neither European nor Czech. When the migrant wave started 10 to 15 years ago, the **Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, and Hungary** had a pragmatic approach. They were condemned for racism and a "merciless" attitude toward migrants, but today, the guest points out, they do not have problems with the weekly burning of cars and shops.

He is glad to live in such a country, and in a Prague neighborhood where legal migrants live. He believes that the European Union, Europe, and even the world, should adopt a lot from the Czech Republic.

sections.subtitle: Neredi u Francuskoj: problem je pristup, a ne siromaštvo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odbacuje socioekonomsko objašnjenje nereda u Francuskoj
sections.content:
Na pitanje o neredima u **Francuskoj**, koji se, kako voditelj kaže, nastavljaju, Omerbegović odgovara: „Oni nikada neće ni prestati.“ Voditelj ironično zahvaljuje na „utješnim“ riječima i pita radi li se o neuspjehu multikulturalizma, neuspjehu integracije ili o pokušaju političkog islamizma.

Gost najprije upozorava da nije pošteno situaciju iz EU-a preslikavati na BiH i obrnuto. Narodi u BiH imaju više zajedničkog nego različitog: isti izgled i vrlo slične tradicije, a razlikuje ih uglavnom religija. Sasvim je drukčije, kaže, kad migrant iz **Nigerije** ili subsaharske Afrike dođe u **Španjolsku** ili **Veliku Britaniju**. Takve ljude je, smatra, vrlo teško integrirati. Kritizira „naivnu ideju“ raširenu na Zapadu posljednjih 20 godina da su sve kulture iste i da svi ljudi imaju iste potrebe i interese.

Voditelj navodi često objašnjenje da su neredi posljedica nedostatka stanova i poslova. Omerbegović ga odlučno odbacuje: socioekonomske faktore „možemo odmah baciti kroz prozor“. Poziva se na sedam godina života u Pragu, gdje je uglavnom bio okružen strancima, ljudima s **Mauricijusa, iz Sirije, s Palaua** i iz mnogih drugih zemalja. U Češkoj, kaže, svi rade, ponašaju se kulturno i nitko ne izlazi na ulice paliti automobile. Iz toga zaključuje da problem nije multikulturalizam sam po sebi, jer u Pragu funkcionira ono što ne funkcionira u Španjolskoj ili Parizu.

Razlika je, po njemu, u **pristupu migraciji**. Važno je znati tko dolazi, odakle i što želi u novoj zemlji. Odaje priznanje državama koje su ljude primale legalno, a ne u golemim valovima. Kao primjer navodi **Poljsku**, „tu super rasističku državu koja nije primila jadne migrante iz Sirije“, a koja je danas jedno od najbrže rastućih gospodarstava u EU-u, možda i u svijetu. Nasuprot tome stavlja **Njemačku**, koja je primila mnogo migranata kao jeftinu radnu snagu, a kojoj danas „baš i nije lijepo“.
sections.subtitle_en: Riots in France: the problem is the approach, not poverty
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest rejects the socioeconomic explanation of the riots in France
sections.content_en:
To the question about the riots in **France**, which, as the host says, are continuing, Omerbegović replies: "They will never even stop." The host ironically thanks him for the "comforting" words and asks whether this is a failure of multiculturalism, a failure of integration, or an attempt of political Islamism.

The guest first warns that it is not fair to project the situation from the EU onto BiH and vice versa. The peoples in BiH have more in common than they have differences: the same appearance and very similar traditions, and what distinguishes them is mainly religion. It is completely different, he says, when a migrant from **Nigeria** or Sub-Saharan Africa arrives in **Spain** or **Great Britain**. Such people, he considers, are very difficult to integrate. He criticizes the "naive idea" widespread in the West over the last 20 years that all cultures are the same and that all people have the same needs and interests.

The host mentions the frequent explanation that the riots are the consequence of a lack of housing and jobs. Omerbegović decisively rejects it: socioeconomic factors "we can throw right out the window". He points to seven years of living in Prague, where he was mostly surrounded by foreigners, people from **Mauritius, from Syria, from Palau**, and from many other countries. In the Czech Republic, he says, everyone works, behaves politely, and no one goes out into the streets to torch cars. From this he concludes that the problem is not multiculturalism per se, because in Prague what does not work in Spain or Paris works.

The difference, according to him, lies in the **approach to migration**. It is important to know who is coming, from where, and what they want in the new country. He gives credit to countries that accepted people legally, and not in enormous waves. As an example he cites **Poland**, "that super racist country that didn't accept poor migrants from Syria", and which is today one of the fastest-growing economies in the EU, perhaps even in the world. In contrast to that, he places **Germany**, which accepted many migrants as cheap labor, and which today "is not really having a nice time".

sections.subtitle: Prvotni grijeh Europe: žigosanje kritičara i uspon AfD-a
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o početnim pogreškama europske migracijske politike
sections.content:
Voditelj iznosi tezu da se briselska birokracija možda ustručavala uvesti strože mjere iz straha od optužbi za islamofobiju i rasizam. Posljedice danas, kaže, snose svi, ne samo kršćani nego i Bošnjaci i muslimani koji žele normalno živjeti, jer u takvim situacijama prije ili kasnije dolazi do generaliziranja da su „svi isti“. Pita gdje se pogriješilo.

Omerbegović smatra da je pogreška napravljena u **početnom pristupu**. Iako postoji mnogo nijansi, ključnim problemom vidi tadašnji „marketing“ koji je bio previše agresivan i nije dopuštao nikakvu raspravu o tome je li dobro primiti toliko ljudi odjednom s drugog kraja svijeta.

Najvećom pogreškom, koju Europa „plaća i dan-danas“, smatra **žigosanje kritičara**. Oni su odmah bili proglašeni islamofobima, groznim ljudima i fašistima koji žele protjerati migrante. Posljedica je, kaže, rast populističkih desnih stranaka, prije svega **AfD-a u Njemačkoj**. Ako se trend nastavi, smatra da je samo pitanje vremena kada će AfD preuzeti vlast.
sections.subtitle_en: Europe's original sin: stigmatizing critics and the rise of the AfD
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the initial mistakes of European migration policy
sections.content_en:
The host presents the thesis that the Brussels bureaucracy may have hesitated to introduce stricter measures out of fear of accusations of Islamophobia and racism. The consequences today, he says, are borne by everyone, not only Christians but also Bosniaks and Muslims who want to live normally, because in such situations sooner or later generalizations arise that "everyone is the same". He asks where the mistake was made.

Omerbegović considers that the mistake was made in the **initial approach**. Although there are many nuances, he sees as the key problem the "marketing" of that time, which was overly aggressive and did not allow any discussion about whether it is good to accept so many people at once from the other side of the world.

The greatest mistake, which Europe "is paying for to this day", he considers to be the **stigmatizing of critics**. They were immediately branded as Islamophobes, awful people, and fascists who want to expel migrants. The consequence, he says, is the growth of populist right-wing parties, above all the **AfD in Germany**. If the trend continues, he thinks it is only a matter of time before the AfD takes power.

sections.subtitle: Dexit i usporedba s Meloni
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje njemačko i talijansko društvo u kontekstu radikalizma
sections.content:
Voditelj spominje medijske napise prema kojima AfD ima spreman **„Dexit“** po uzoru na Brexit i pita ne urušava li se time Europa. Zanima ga je li AfD doista toliko radikalan ili će se dogoditi isto što i s **Meloni**, koja je „svašta govorila“, a na kraju, kako kaže, izvela vojsku na ulice.

Omerbegović upozorava da je riječ o dva različita društva. Njemačko je društvo u 80-ak godina od kraja Drugog svjetskog rata imalo drukčiju putanju od talijanskog i ostatka Europe. U Njemačkoj postoji snažan **strah od ponavljanja prošlosti**, pa su Nijemci vrlo oprezni prema svakom radikalizmu, ili barem prema onome što sami nazivaju radikalizmom.

AfD ipak smatra vrlo radikalnom strankom za njemačke standarde. Do sada nije bilo stranke koja je tako otvoreno govorila stvari koje podsjećaju na autoritarni rječnik. Istodobno ponavlja da je sve to **reakcija na probleme** s kojima se suočavaju Europa i velik dio Zapada.
sections.subtitle_en: Dexit and comparison with Meloni
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares German and Italian society in the context of radicalism
sections.content_en:
The host mentions media reports according to which the AfD has **"Dexit"** ready, modeled after Brexit, and asks whether Europe is not collapsing as a result. He wonders whether the AfD is indeed that radical or if the same will happen as with **Meloni**, who "said all sorts of things" and in the end, as he says, deployed the army onto the streets.

Omerbegović warns that these are two different societies. German society in the roughly 80 years since the end of World War II has had a different trajectory from the Italian one and the rest of Europe. In Germany there is a strong **fear of repeating the past**, so Germans are very cautious toward any radicalism, or at least toward what they themselves call radicalism.

Yet he considers the AfD a very radical party by German standards. Until now there has been no party that has so openly said things reminiscent of an authoritarian vocabulary. At the same time, he repeats that all this is a **reaction to the problems** facing Europe and a large part of the West.

sections.subtitle: Nema brzih rješenja, a Poljska iznenađuje
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje gospodarski rast Poljske i Njemačke
sections.content:
Na izravno pitanje kako riješiti migracijsko pitanje, Omerbegović kaže da odgovor mora biti vrlo precizan. Mnogi bi, kaže, prebrzo odgovorili:

- protjerajte sve ilegalne migrante,
- ograničite migracije,
- potaknite prirodni prirast domaćeg stanovništva.

Nije siguran koliko bi to bilo učinkovito. Smatra da je Zapad došao do točke u kojoj su potrebni **konkretni, provedivi koraci** koji uzimaju u obzir i ekonomiju i moralna pitanja. Priznaje da ne zna brzo rješenje i dodaje da je na narodu da izabere politiku koja će ga ponuditi.

Voditelj suprotstavlja dvije slike: vojsku na ulicama **Milana** i policijski sat u **Parizu** s jedne strane, a s druge poljskog europarlamentarca čije ime, priznaje, ne zna izgovoriti, a koji se hvali „nulom“ migranata. Poljskoj se, kaže, ne može mnogo zamjeriti jer štiti svoje granice.

Omerbegović dodaje da nije stvar samo u granicama. Da se ovaj razgovor vodio prije desetak godina, bilo bi mnogo predviđanja o tome kako će Poljska izgledati, a nitko nije zamišljao da će postati jedno od najbrže rastućih gospodarstava u Europi. Tada se govorilo da je potrebno mnogo „uvoznog“ stanovništva kako bi se revitaliziralo gospodarstvo i BDP povećao za dva do tri posto. Danas se, ističe, događa suprotno: deset godina kasnije **Njemačka je u minusu, a Poljska raste**. Budućnost je, zaključuje, neizvjesna.
sections.subtitle_en: There are no quick fixes, and Poland surprises
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares the economic growth of Poland and Germany
sections.content_en:
To the direct question of how to solve the migration issue, Omerbegović says that the answer must be very precise. Many, he says, would answer too quickly:

- expel all illegal migrants,
- restrict migration,
- boost the natural increase of the domestic population.

He is not sure how effective that would be. He believes that the West has reached a point where **concrete, feasible steps** are needed that take into account both the economy and moral questions. He admits that he does not know a quick solution and adds that it is up to the people to choose the politics that will offer it.

The host contrasts two pictures: the military on the streets of **Milan** and a curfew in **Paris** on the one hand, and on the other a Polish MEP whose name, he admits, he does not know how to pronounce, and who boasts of "zero" migrants. Poland, he says, cannot be faulted much because it protects its borders.

Omerbegović adds that it is not just a matter of borders. If this conversation had taken place ten or so years ago, there would have been many predictions about what Poland would look like, and no one imagined that it would become one of the fastest-growing economies in Europe. At that time it was said that a lot of "imported" population was needed to revitalize the economy and increase GDP by two to three percent. Today, he points out, the opposite is happening: ten years later **Germany is in the red, and Poland is growing**. The future, he concludes, is uncertain.

sections.subtitle: Ratovi koji svake godine „samo što nisu počeli“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava sjećanja američkog prijatelja na hladnoratovske vježbe
sections.content:
Voditelj pita je li sve to dio „legendarne agende“ i dodaje da ga plaši kako podcasti, mainstream mediji i društvene mreže neprestano najavljuju sukobe 2028. ili 2030. Takve se najave, kaže, sada čitaju kao vremenska prognoza.

Omerbegović odgovara anegdotom. Ima prijatelja Amerikanca u šezdesetima, pred mirovinom, koji mu je pričao o djetinjstvu 70-ih i 80-ih. U američkim školama gotovo su se svaki tjedan održavale vježbe, kao da će **Sovjetski Savez** svakog trenutka baciti nuklearnu bombu.

Gost smatra da je ljudima u prirodi razmišljati u **apokaliptičnim scenarijima**. O neizbježnom sukobu u Europi govori se još od kraja posljednjeg velikog rata, a on se još nije dogodio. Predviđanje budućnosti kod tako složenih tema, s mnogo nepoznanica, smatra vrlo nezahvalnim. Sebe opisuje kao optimista i kaže da nije sve tako crno.
sections.subtitle_en: Wars that every year "are just about to start"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts memories of an American friend regarding Cold War drills
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether all this is part of the "legendary agenda" and adds that it scares him how podcasts, mainstream media, and social networks are constantly announcing conflicts in 2028 or 2030. Such announcements, he says, are now read like a weather forecast.

Omerbegović responds with an anecdote. He has an American friend in his sixties, near retirement, who told him about his childhood in the 1970s and 1980s. In American schools, drills were held almost every week, as if the **Soviet Union** were about to drop a nuclear bomb at any moment.

The guest considers that it is in human nature to think in **apocalyptic scenarios**. An inevitable conflict in Europe has been talked about ever since the end of the last great war, and it has not yet happened. Predicting the future on such complex topics, with many unknowns, he considers very unrewarding. He describes himself as an optimist and says that not everything is so bleak.

sections.subtitle: Digitalni novac i čepovi na bocama: tromost, a ne zavjera
sections.screenshot_description: Gost odbacuje teorije zavjere o digitalnom novcu i govori o briselskoj birokraciji
sections.content:
Voditelj nabraja: neredi, „pola Europe gori“, rat Ukrajine i Rusije, napetosti oko Indije i Kine, a briselska administracija u tom trenutku donosi uredbu o **digitalnom novcu**. Sebe u šali naziva teoretičarom zavjere i strahuje da je riječ o apsolutnoj kontroli, jer je svakome tko je imalo informatički pismen jasno da se ljude može pratiti u svakom trenutku. „Što će mi još digitalne pare?“, pita.

Omerbegović priznaje da nije sklon teorijama zavjere. Na budućnost gleda pozitivno jer, kao ni u BiH, ništa nije „zapisano u kamenu“. Kao primjer navodi **Latinsku Ameriku**: tko bi rekao da će se nakon toliko godina razgovarati o slobodnim izborima u **Venezueli**, ili o AfD-u u Njemačkoj?

Europska unija, prema njegovu mišljenju, ide smjerom koji sama smatra najboljim. To nije ciljani smjer opće kontrole, nego smjer **trome birokracije koja će se s vremenom sama pročistiti**, jer glomazna Europa ne može dugo podnositi birokraciju koja se bavi naizgled nebitnim pitanjima. Podsjeća na internetski mim u kojem Tesla u Americi lansira leteći automobil, a EU se bavi **čepovima na bocama**. Voditelj dodaje i papirnate slamke.

Omerbegović u tome vidi i dobru stranu: to je posljedica činjenice da Europa desetljećima nije doživjela strah od rata. Radije bi se, kaže, bavio čepovima nego razmišljao o izradi oružja. Voditelj mu tada predbacuje da se Europljani bave čepovima i slamkama, a istodobno im se servira priča o sukobu 2030.
sections.subtitle_en: Digital money and bottle caps: sluggishness, not conspiracy
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest rejects conspiracy theories about digital money and talks about Brussels bureaucracy
sections.content_en:
The host lists: riots, "half of Europe is burning", the war between Ukraine and Russia, tensions around India and China, and the Brussels administration at that moment adopts a regulation on **digital money**. He jokingly calls himself a conspiracy theorist and fears that this is about absolute control, because to anyone who is even slightly computer literate it is clear that people can be tracked at any moment. "What do I need digital cash for as well?", he asks.

Omerbegović admits that he is not inclined toward conspiracy theories. He looks at the future positively because, just as in BiH, nothing is "written in stone". As an example he cites **Latin America**: who would have thought that after so many years there would be discussions about free elections in **Venezuela**, or about the AfD in Germany?

The European Union, in his opinion, is moving in the direction that it itself considers best. That is not a targeted direction of total control, but a direction of **sluggish bureaucracy that will purge itself over time**, because a bulky Europe cannot tolerate for long a bureaucracy that deals with seemingly trivial issues. He recalls an internet meme in which Tesla in America launches a flying car, while the EU deals with **bottle caps**. The host also adds paper straws.

Omerbegović sees a good side to this as well: it is a consequence of the fact that Europe has not experienced the fear of war for decades. He would rather, he says, deal with caps than think about manufacturing weapons. The host then reproaches him that Europeans are dealing with caps and straws, while at the same time being served the story of a conflict in 2030.

sections.subtitle: Poziv na polemiku i optimistična odjava
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj predlaže budući susret gosta i Fatmira Ali Spahića u podcastu
sections.content:
Na voditeljevu primjedbu o 2030. Omerbegović odgovara s humorom. Nada se da će se njih dvojica vidjeti u podcastu i 2030., pa razgovarati o tome kako su četiri godine ranije imali suprotna mišljenja. Uz smiješak dodaje da će možda netko od njih tada biti u zatvoru „jer izgovara zlo misao“.

Voditelj zatim predlaže da se gost jednom u studiju sretne s **Fatmirom Ali Spahićem** i da njih dvojica vode polemiku. Ograđuje se da možda nije korektno spominjati čovjeka koji nije prisutan, ali vjeruje da bi Ali Spahić pristao. Omerbegović odgovara: „Zašto da ne?“ i izražava nadu da će se susret ostvariti.

Na kraju se gost opisuje kao „velikog optimista“. Voditelj ga moli da pozdravi Bosnu i poželi sve najbolje njoj i Europi. Omerbegović zahvaljuje na pozivu i žali što ne mogu razgovarati još sat vremena, a ostale teme ostavlja za neki budući razgovor.
sections.subtitle_en: Invitation to a debate and an optimistic sign-off
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host suggests a future meeting between the guest and Fatmir Ali Spahić on the podcast
sections.content_en:
To the host's remark about 2030, Omerbegović responds with humor. He hopes that the two of them will see each other on the podcast in 2030 as well, and talk about how four years earlier they had opposite opinions. With a smile he adds that perhaps one of them will then be in prison "for uttering thoughtcrime".

The host then suggests that the guest meet once in the studio with **Fatmir Ali Spahić** and that the two of them hold a debate. He hedges that it might not be fair to mention a man who is not present, but believes that Ali Spahić would agree. Omerbegović replies: "Why not?" and expresses hope that the meeting will take place.

At the end, the guest describes himself as a "great optimist". The host asks him to say hello to Bosnia and wish all the best to it and Europe. Omerbegović thanks him for the invitation and regrets that they cannot talk for another hour, leaving other topics for some future conversation.
